properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-20.

HIS WORDS: "add gaps that need to be closed to increments/epochs."

WHY IT LANDS EXACTLY WHERE IT SHOULD: this design carries 89 open gaps, 85 of which have never been put to anybody. Two of them were surfaced and answered today only because he said, in as many words, that he does not like something identified and then dropped. A list of 89 that endures and is skimmed is durable and useless at the same time. Scheduling is the mechanism that turns a standing list into work with a moment attached.

⚠️ THE MODELLING PROBLEM, stated first because it shapes every option: A GAP IS NOT A NODE. Gaps are COMPUTED from the condition every run — that is why gap:4e24a202aa6f1737 carried the same id this morning and this afternoon, and why it disappears the moment the condition is fixed rather than needing to be closed by hand. That property is valuable and should not be traded away. But it means there is nothing to hang a SCHEDULED_FOR edge on, and SCHEDULED_FOR is declared `from: [Capability, Requirement]` only.

OPTIONS, none chosen:
  (a) SCHEDULE THE QUESTION, not the gap. `gap_to_prompt` already mints a durable `question:<id>` node when a gap is put to somebody, and open_questions already tracks it until answered. Widening SCHEDULED_FOR to accept a Question would let 'these twelve questions get answered in increment 4' be said, with no change to how gaps are computed. Cheapest, and it reuses a node that already exists for exactly the purpose of making a gap durable.
  (b) SCHEDULE THE AFFECTED NODE. Every gap names `affected_ids`; scheduling those is already possible where they are Capabilities or Requirements. Weak: the gap and the node are different things, and a component can carry several unrelated gaps.
  (c) A GAP BECOMES A NODE when somebody accepts it as work — promotion rather than computation. Strongest expressive power, and the biggest change: it creates a second source of truth about whether the gap is still real, which is precisely what the computed-every-run design avoids.
  (d) ACKNOWLEDGE, which already exists — `acknowledge_gap` records a reviewed judgement with a reason. But acknowledging says 'we looked and accept this', not 'we will fix this in increment 4'. Those are different answers and only one of them is a plan.

RECOMMENDATION IF ASKED, and it is a finding rather than a decision: (a). It needs no change to gap computation, it reuses the Question node that already turns a computed gap into something durable and addressed to a person, and it composes with the work-package idea — a package could then hold questions as well as capabilities.

CONNECTED TO A DEFECT ALREADY ON THE RECORD: `fact:a-capability-delivered-as-a-model-change-can-never-be-reported-delivered`. Closing a gap is almost always MODEL work, not a file, so if gaps become schedulable before delivery stops requiring an artifact, every scheduled gap would sit `outstanding` forever — the new mechanism would inherit the existing blind spot on day one. These two should be answered together, or the delivery one first.

RELATED: dec:idea-lining-work-up-in-increments-should-be-the-default-not-a-skill-you-remember, dec:idea-an-increment-can-be-sliced-into-work-packages-with-an-owner.
properties.name: OPEN — can a gap that needs closing be scheduled into an increment, the way a capability or requirement is?
